small_guidance:
- The gemm_lse_kernel materializes a [BLOCK_M, O_CONST] = [64, 1024] fp32 accumulator (256 KB) which exceeds the 100KB SMEM limit on 4090. Drop BLOCK_M to ≤16 and remove the num_warps=8 / num_stages=3 configs that blow up SMEM; cap configs at BLOCK_M=8 or 16 with num_stages=2.
- Also reduce BLOCK_H to 32 in the surviving configs so the [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_H] Y tile and [BLOCK_H, O_CONST]=[32,1024] W tile stay within budget; pre-filter the autotune list to only configs where BLOCK_M*O_CONST*4 + BLOCK_H*O_CONST*4 < 90KB.
- Pass O as a tl.constexpr only when small (≤1024) — keep current shape but add a guard so the launcher prunes oversized configs.
large_guidance:
- Stop holding the full O dimension in registers. Redesign gemm_lse as a two-pass online-LSE kernel: pass 1 streams O in BLOCK_O=128 tiles, computing per-row running max m and running sum s using the online softmax recurrence (s_new = s_old*exp(m_old - m_new) + sum(exp(z - m_new))), so the accumulator is just two [BLOCK_M] vectors plus one [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_O] tile. This eliminates the SMEM blow-up and lets BLOCK_M scale to 64-128.
- Inside each O-tile, do the full GEMM-over-H loop with tl.dot using BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_O=128, BLOCK_H=32-64 — a standard tiled GEMM with the LSE recurrence as the epilogue. Bias add stays fused before the max update.
- Alternative: split-K style — one program per (M-tile, O-tile) writes the partial logits to a scratch [M, O] buffer, then a second tiny kernel does the row-wise LSE. Simpler but adds a global write/read of M*O floats; only worth it if the online-recurrence version is hard to tune.
